name: Austrian Dominoes
description: Austrian Dominoes is a unique European variant traditionally played with a Double-Eight set. Its most striking features are the complete removal of all double tiles and a 'brick-layer' tableau formation where tiles are matched side-by-side rather than end-to-end. It is a strategic draw game where players value 'heavier' tiles early in the round.

content.text: Austrian Dominoes is a unique European variant traditionally played with a Double-Eight set. Its most striking features are the complete removal of all double tiles and a 'brick-layer' tableau formation where tiles are matched side-by-side rather than end-to-end. It is a strategic draw game where players value 'heavier' tiles early in the round.
Documented in Vienna as early as 1830, Austrian Dominoes reflects the Central European preference for Double-Eight sets over the more common Double-Six set used in the West.
36 tiles. To prepare, take a Double-Eight set (45 tiles) and discard all 9 doubles (0-0, 1-1... up to 8-8).
2 players: 8-9 tiles each. 3 players: 7 tiles each. 4 players: 8 tiles each. Remaining tiles form the 'Stamm' (Boneyard).

items.text: Buki: A 4-player block version where all titles are dealt out and no drawing is allowed.
